grade.first_issue: In Case 3, the claim that Mulan can force an angle of 2θ merely because 2θ≤180° is unsupported and false in general. Consequently, the assertion that every θ<90° is winning does not follow.
grade.summary: The final classification is false, so Rule A caps the score at 2. For example, θ=70° is included by the submission but is not winning. Shan-Yu may start with {35°,35°,110°}. Calling a triangle safe when none of its angles is a positive integer multiple of 70°, this triangle is safe; after any cut, at least one child remains safe, since if both children acquired such a multiple, comparison of their new angles would force either 180° or a parent angle to be a multiple of 70°, a contradiction. Thus Shan-Yu can avoid 70° forever. Correcting the solution requires the new invariant and the discrete classification θ=180°/n, n≥2.
strengths: The argument excluding θ>90° is essentially correct: starting with all angles below θ, no cut can make both retained options contain an angle at least θ.
The one-move strategy for θ=90° is essentially correct after choosing the two acute angles as the base angles.

errors.description: The claimed answer 0°<θ≤90° incorrectly includes values such as θ=70°. The actual answer is the discrete set θ=180°/n for integers n≥2.

The entire sufficiency argument for θ<90° rests on unproved assertions that a right angle permits forcing any smaller target and that Mulan can force 2θ. Repeatedly peeling θ from one angle guarantees θ in only one child and does not address Shan-Yu's choices.
